title: One Agent or a Team?
subtitle: How to pick the right pattern for your agentic AI system
intro: You asked an AI to plan a trip. Should one smart assistant do it all, or a team of specialists split the work?
takeaway: Pick your agent pattern by task complexity, latency, cost, and risk — not hype.

sections.heading: Analogy: one chef vs a kitchen crew
sections.body:
Think of a food truck with one chef. One person takes the order, cooks, and serves. It's fast and cheap.

A big restaurant has a crew: a host, line cooks, a pastry chef. Slower to coordinate, but better for a complex menu.

An agentic AI system is the same choice: one agent doing the whole workflow, or multiple agents orchestrated together. That choice shapes everything next.

sections.heading: Why it exists: to match pattern to problem
sections.body:
An agent design pattern is a framework for organizing components and orchestrating agents to hit a goal with some autonomy.

You use it for open-ended, multi-step, knowledge-intensive tasks that need real-time data — not simple chat.

Your save says choose by requirements: use single-agent when speed and low cost matter; use multi-agent when accuracy on complex tasks matters more than latency.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when the pattern doesn't fit
sections.body:
A single agent fails on complex work — it forgets steps and makes more mistakes.

A multi-agent team fails differently: every extra agent means extra inference calls, so cost and latency climb fast.

For high-stakes tasks, both fail without human-in-the-loop oversight. Pick cheap and fast, or accurate and costly — you can't have both.

steps.narration: Start with your goal and workflow.
Ask: is it open-ended and multi-step?
If simple, one agent is faster and cheaper.
If complex, a team of agents is more accurate.
More agents means more inference calls, cost, and latency.
Add human oversight for high-stakes decisions.

quiz.q: When should you use an AI agent instead of a simple assistant?
options: For open-ended, multi-step tasks needing autonomy and real-time data
quiz.why: Your save says agents excel at goal-focused, autonomous, knowledge-intensive workflows, not simple assistive tasks.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x with a multi-agent pattern?
options: Cost and latency explode from many inference calls
Human oversight is no longer needed
quiz.why: Each agent adds inference calls. At scale, cost and latency are the first tradeoffs to break.

quiz.q: You need high accuracy for a complex legal review. What pattern fits best?
quiz.why: Complex tasks favor multi-agent for accuracy, and high-stakes tasks need human oversight per your save.
